title: Epoch-mean searches miss long dust events when transition times scale with duration
abstract: We test the duration range of two-epoch mean-photometry searches for dust dimming. We prove that the magnitude difference of two mean fluxes is at most the largest magnitude slope times the maximum quantile separation of their weighted observation times. The coefficient is sharp. For the published trapezoid shape with 15-percent ingress and egress, any 0.5-mag event longer than 82.2 years cannot pass a 0.3-mag difference cut with epochs inside 2010-2017.4. Uniform PS1 and Gaia windows tighten this sufficient ceiling to 50.8 years. Exact flux integration gives a 6.62-year detection window for an eight-year event, but zero for a 50-year event. A constructed duration mixture gives the same expected count while the total onset rate changes by a factor of 1000. The prior eight-year-template rate remains scoped to that template. These are analytic and synthetic results, not new observations or a measured duration distribution. Fixed positive weights, noiseless same-band means and transitions that scale with event duration are required. Original code, aggregate results, proof, figures and source hashes are included.

display.caption: Exact uniform-window experiment for the published scaled trapezoid model. Long smooth events fall below the difference cut. These are synthetic signals, not new survey data.
